questions.question: Why did so many trees in the first planting die?
keyFacts: A late May 2019 frost killed 17 of the first 38 trees
The nursery trees were raised in a milder inland climate and had already broken bud
traps: The trees died only because of bad weather

questions.question: Would frost cloth have saved the 2019 trees?
keyFacts: A 2020 test found covered and uncovered trees suffered almost the same damage
Local stock, not frost cloth, was the answer
traps: Frost cloth would have saved or did save the trees

questions.question: How did the Circle reduce tree losses after the first year?
keyFacts: Grafting cuttings from old local survivor trees onto hardy rootstock
Only 9 of 102 grafted trees were lost, under nine percent

questions.question: What happened at the harbour roundabout site?
keyFacts: Only 4 of 14 trees planted in 2021 were alive in 2024
Road salt and truck spray killed them
The land was given back to the council in 2023

questions.question: What are the Orchard Circle's three rules?
keyFacts: A named person waters each new tree for its first two summers
Pruning happens only on one fixed Saturday in late February (Cutting Day)
Fruit is never sold
traps: Fruit is sold or an offer from the cider maker or supermarket was accepted

questions.question: Does the Circle sell its fruit?
keyFacts: No; it refused offers from a cider maker and a supermarket
Unpicked fruit goes to the food bank and the school kitchen
traps: Fruit is sold or an offer from the cider maker or supermarket was accepted

questions.question: How big were the harvests, and how reliable are those numbers?
keyFacts: About 0.8 tonnes in 2022, 1.9 in 2023, and 3.1 in 2024
Only the donated portion was weighed; passer-by picking was estimated
traps: The harvest figures are exact or precisely measured

questions.question: Did the orchard end up costing the town nothing?
keyFacts: No; the council pays about 600 euros a year for volunteer insurance
It still costs less than the roughly 1,500 euros a year of mowing it replaced
traps: The orchard costs the town nothing or fully met its zero-cost goal

questions.question: How much did the orchard cost and where did the money come from?
keyFacts: About 9,400 euros over five years
Mostly from yearly sales of spare grafted saplings, plus small donations

questions.question: Who started the orchard, and who runs Cutting Day now?
keyFacts: Odile Fenn, a retired ferry engineer, proposed it in January 2019
Three of Ravi Osei's former pupils now run Cutting Day
